resources.string: The machine will calibrate the thickness measurement system automatically with the calibration target. Redo this calibration after you have reassembled the machine, replaced the toolhead or if you find the thickness measurement is inaccurate.

For 4-axis machining, you need to locate the central axis of the Rotary Module using a cylinder material. Completing this calibration allows you to start a laser job properly via inputting the material’s diameter.

1. Hang the black PLA filament that comes with the machine onto the left filament holder, and feed the filament into the left guide tube until it reaches the other end. \n2. Insert the filament into the left filament entry on the Dual Extrusion Module until you can feel the filament is gripped and being pulled in. \n3. Insert the guide tube into the left filament entry.

1. Hang the white PLA filament that comes with the machine onto the right filament holder, and feed the filament into the right guide tube until it reaches the other end. \n2. Insert the filament into the right filament entry on the Dual Extrusion Module until you can feel the filament is gripped and being pulled in. \n3. Insert the guide tube into the right filament entry.
Observe if any filament is coming out of the left nozzle. \nIf yes, then the filament is loaded and you can tap Continue. \nIf not, tap Load Filament to load again.
Observe if any filament is coming out of the right nozzle. \nIf yes, then the filament is loaded and you can tap Done to move on. \nIf not, tap Load Filament to load again.

The calibration models will be printed again. Clean the build plate before you proceed.。

Manually lower the left nozzle of the toolhead against the 3D printing platform’s surface with the calibration card until you feel slight resistance when you pull out the calibration card, and it should be wrinkled when you push it forward.

The machine will print one calibration model for X and Y orientation each. You need to find the best pair of lines in the printed models to calibrate the offsets of the two nozzles in the X and Y orientations.
The left and right nozzle will automatically touch the 3D printing platform in turn to calibrate the Z offset so that the two nozzles can work at the right and same height when printing.

Submit the Z offset of the current position as the left nozzle’s initial printing height.

Place the calibration card between the left toolhead and the heated bed, and tap Next. Then, adjust the Z offset until you feel slight resistance when pulling out the calibration card, and it should be wrinkled when you push it forward.
Turn the front-right thumbwheel under the heated bed to adjust the Z offset of the left toolhead at the right point, and calibrate it with the calibration card.

If there will be no more calibration next, clean the heated bed surface and install the PEI glass plate back onto the bed.

The nozzles and the bed have been heated. Tap Next to proceed.
Rotate the left leveling wheel under the bed to move the orange bar to the midpoint. If you don’t see any orange bar, keep rotating as prompted.
Rotate the right leveling wheel under the bed to move the orange bar to the midpoint. If you don’t see any orange bar, keep rotating as prompted.
The two extruders will touch the heated bed in sequence, and you need to calibrate the Z offset of the right extruder to ensure that the two extruders work at the right and same height.
Tighten the two screws on the right extruder.\n\nIf there will be no more calibration next, clean the heated bed surface and install the PEI glass plate back onto the bed.
Tighten the two screws on the right extruder.
Loosen the two screws on the right extruder by one turn with the H2.0 hex key, and tap Next.
Rotate the thumb wheel of the right extruder to move the orange bar to the midpoint. If you don’t see any orange bar, keep rotating as prompted.
The two extruders will touch the heated bed in sequence to obtain and calibrate their offsets in the X and Y orientations automatically.
The machine is obtaining the data and calibrating automatically...
The X and Y offsets of the two extruders have been calibrated.
The machine will print a built-in model with both extruders. By observing the model with the prompts on the Touchscreen, you can check if the offset calibrations are successful.
Make sure the PEI glass plate has been installed onto the heated bed.
Tap Go to Load to load two PLA filaments of distinct colors (like orange and white) into the extruders. \n\nIf the filaments are already loaded, tap Print.

If the surfaces of differently colored areas are flush with each other, then the Z Offset Calibration is successful. If not, you need to do the calibration again.\n\nTap Next to check the XY Offset Calibration results.

Remove the model from the PEI glass plate, and try breaking off the outer squares from the model. If the four squares can all be broken off (not necessarily completely), then the XY Offset Calibration is successful. If not, you need to do the calibration again.
Step 2: Hang the filament onto the filament holder, and feed the filament into the filament entry until it protrudes from the other end of the tube.
Step 3: Push the toggle backward and hold; then insert the filament into the extruder until you feel resistance (taking the left extruder for example).
Step 4: Set a target temperature and tap Heat.
Step 5: Tap Load (the extruder will automatically move to an appropriate position to start loading, if necessary).
Step 6: When the filament oozes out of the nozzle, tap Stop Loading.
Step 7: Insert the guide tube into the extruder and then snap it into the tube clip. Finally, reinstall the top panel.
